slides.title: Introduction to std::thread
slides.prompt: C++11 introduced std::thread in the <thread> header to represent execution threads. When a std::thread object is constructed with a callable, a new thread of execution is spawned immediately.

slides.title: Joining a Thread
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing method name that blocks the current thread until the target thread finishes execution.
slides.codeSnippet:
std::thread t(workerFunction);
t.___(); // Blocks until workerFunction completes

slides.title: Thread Destruction without Join or Detach
slides.prompt: What happens if a std::thread object is destroyed while it is still joinable (neither join() nor detach() was called)?
options: std::terminate is called, abruptly crashing the program
The thread automatically detaches and runs in the background
The thread is automatically joined at destruction
A runtime exception is thrown that can be caught
slides.correctAnswer: std::terminate is called, abruptly crashing the program

slides.title: Detaching Threads
slides.prompt: Fill in the method name used to separate the thread object from the execution thread, allowing it to run independently.
slides.codeSnippet:
std::thread t(backgroundTask);
t.___(); // Thread now runs independently in the background

slides.title: Checking Joinability
slides.prompt: Which method checks whether a std::thread object represents an active thread of execution?

slides.title: Passing Parameters to Threads
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard wrapper function needed to pass parameters by reference to a thread function.

slides.title: Moving Threads
slides.prompt: Which statement regarding std::thread ownership is correct?
options: std::thread is move-only; it cannot be copied
std::thread can be both copied and moved freely
std::thread can be copied but not moved
std::thread cannot be moved or copied
slides.correctAnswer: std::thread is move-only; it cannot be copied
